prompt:
You are scouting a single volleyball match from a fixed camera.

CRITICAL: Analyze ONLY the main court in the foreground. Ignore background matches completely.

The vertical net divides the court. For the `side` field, output 'left' if the contacting player is on the left side of the net, or 'right' if they are on the right side.
IMPORTANT: Log the side where the player HITS the ball, NOT where the ball lands! If a right-side player hits a winner that lands on the left floor, log a `kill` for the RIGHT side.

This clip begins at {start:.2f} seconds and runs for 6 seconds.
WARNING: Clips often start MID-RALLY. The first contact you see might be a receive or dig. DO NOT assume it is a serve. A serve requires a visible toss.

MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE EVENTS (ONE PER CONTACT):
Output EXACTLY ONE event type per physical ball contact. Choose the single best fit.
- If an attack wins the rally, label it ONLY as `kill`.
- If a block wins the point, label it ONLY as `block`.

ACTION DEFINITIONS:
DO NOT REPORT EVERY CONTACT. You MUST skip regular sets, non-scoring blocks, and dead-time passing.
  serve   - STARTS a rally. ONLY report if you clearly see the player toss the ball from a stationary hold behind the back line. If the ball is already flying over the net, it is NEVER a serve.
  receive - a defensive pass handling the opponent's serve, keeping the ball on the SAME side of the net.
  dig     - a defensive pass handling the opponent's attack, keeping the ball on the SAME side of the net.
  set     - an assist pass. ONLY report if it directly sets up a point-winning kill (even if the kill itself happens just after the clip ends). SKIP ALL OTHER SETS.
  attack  - ANY contact that sends the ball OVER the net to the opponent's side. Digs and receives MUST NOT go over the net.
  kill    - an offensive hit that wins the rally. Logged for the attacker who hit it.
  block   - a block AT THE NET. ONLY report if it immediately wins the point (a stuff block).

DEAD TIME VETO: Ignore practice hits, practice serves, and post-rally bounces. Contacts after the ball hits the floor are NEVER valid events! A serve is ONLY real if the receiving team is fully in a ready defensive formation.

For each contact give:
  t       - the EXACT moment of physical impact in ABSOLUTE MATCH SECONDS ({start:.2f} + offset). Estimate the offset carefully to one decimal place (e.g. 2.3). Deduplication relies on precise timing!
  type    - one of the seven above
  side    - "left" or "right" (where the player made contact)
  number  - the contacting player's jersey number as a string, or null if unreadable. Do not guess.
  error   - true if this contact was an error (into the net, out of bounds)
  point   - true ONLY for the final contact if it directly WON the point for the team that made the contact (like a kill or unreturnable serve). NEVER true for regular passes!

Return an empty list if no valid play happens.
